documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Annual physical, 57F.

Onc: R vulvar SCC IB s/p excision 1/2024, NED at gyn onc 10/24 and gyn 1/25. Next gyn onc April.
COPD: winter was okay, used albuterol more during the January cold, no steroids or antibiotics, no urgent visits. Back to ~2x/week.
HTN: on amlodipine 5.
Tobacco: 1 ppd, ~32 pack-years. Not ready.

ROS negative otherwise. No bleeding, no new lumps.

Exam: vitals per flowsheet, BP fine. NAD. No adenopathy cervical/supraclavicular/inguinal. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs prolonged expiration, no wheeze, no crackles. Abd soft. Ext no edema.

PHQ-2 0, AUDIT-C 2.

A/P
1. COPD GOLD 2, stable, same regimen.
2. HTN controlled.
3. Vulvar SCC surveillance per gyn onc/gyn.
4. Tobacco: advised; declines meds or a quit date.
5. HM: labs today. Mammo 11/24 neg, LDCT 12/24 neg - both repeat in fall/winter. Colonoscopy 2028. Cervical per gyn (NILM 7/24).

RTC September.

documents.title: Question
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi, I'm probably overreacting but I have been having some spotting and bleeding on and off since around November. Not every day, sometimes a week or two goes by. I was supposed to see my gynecologist in April and I pushed it because of work. Should I be worried? Evelyn

documents.title: Telephone Call
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Called pt re: last night's message. ~6 months of intermittent vaginal bleeding/spotting, postmenopausal. Some of the earlier spotting was after intercourse, but no intercourse for the last few months and it continues. No pain, no vulvar itching, no groin lumps. Not on any hormones.

With her vulvar SCC history this needs a gyn exam now, not in a few months. Called her gynecologist's office directly - they will see her 5/18, first available with her own gynecologist; they'll call if something opens sooner. Gyn onc office aware. Told her plainly that bleeding after menopause always needs to be looked at, and with her history it's especially important not to wait. She agreed. Will watch for the note.

OUTSIDE GYNECOLOGY
Date of service: 05/18/2026
Re: Evelyn Murphy, DOB 11/28/1967

58-year-old with a history of right vulvar squamous cell carcinoma (stage IB, excised 01/2024), seen sooner at her PCP's request. For six months she has had irregular postmenopausal bleeding along with spotting after intercourse; she has not been sexually active recently.

PMH: COPD, hypertension, tobacco dependence. Condylomata treated in the past. Lap chole 2010.
Medications: albuterol as needed, tiotropium 18 mcg daily, amlodipine 5 mg daily.
Allergies: NKDA.
Family: mother cervical cancer at 42; father lung cancer at 58; sister CIN II.
Social: smoker, 30 pack-years.

Exam: Groins without palpable adenopathy. Vulva: healed right excision scar, no lesion. Speculum: a 2 cm ulcerative lesion on the posterior vaginal wall. Cervix appears normal. Bimanual and the rest of the pelvic exam unremarkable.

Procedure: biopsy of the posterior vaginal wall lesion under local anesthesia, sent to pathology. Minimal bleeding, Monsel's applied.

Impression: Posterior vaginal wall ulcerative lesion in a patient with prior vulvar SCC; concerning for malignancy. Will call with pathology and coordinate with gynecologic oncology.

documents.title: Gynecologic Oncology Consultation
documents.author: gynecologic oncology
documents.body:
GYNECOLOGIC ONCOLOGY CONSULTATION - 06/02/2026
Patient: Evelyn Murphy (DOB 11/28/1967)
Known to us: right vulvar SCC, FIGO IB, radical local excision with SLN biopsy 01/09/2024, NED through 10/2025.

New problem: posterior vaginal wall lesion biopsied by her gynecologist 05/18/2026, invasive SCC. Six months of intermittent postmenopausal bleeding.

Medications: tiotropium, albuterol prn, amlodipine 5 mg. Allergies: NKDA. Current smoker.

Exam: No inguinal or femoral adenopathy. Vulva: healed right scar, no lesion; the vulva is separate from the vaginal lesion. Speculum: 2 cm ulcerated lesion on the posterior vaginal wall with healing biopsy site. Cervix normal in appearance. Rectovaginal exam: lesion mobile and confined to the vaginal wall, no extension into the paravaginal tissue or rectovaginal septum.

Assessment: Squamous cell carcinoma of the vagina, clinically confined to the vaginal wall (FIGO stage I, pending imaging). Vulva and cervix are not involved.

Plan:
1. CT chest, abdomen and pelvis with contrast.
2. If no nodal or distant disease: wide local excision of the posterior vaginal wall lesion (partial vaginectomy). Discussed the alternative of radiation; given the small, mobile lesion she prefers surgery.
3. Pre-op clearance with PCP.
4. Smoking cessation before and after surgery, again.

Gynecologic Oncology

documents.title: Pre-operative Evaluation
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
PRE-OP
Planned: wide local excision of posterior vaginal wall lesion (partial vaginectomy), gyn onc, 6/23/26, general anesthesia, same-day discharge expected.

Background: vaginal SCC on biopsy 5/18/26, clinically stage I; staging CT 6/4 negative (no nodes, no mets, no lung nodule). Prior R vulvar SCC IB, excised 1/2024 without complication - did well with GA then.

COPD GOLD 2 (FEV1 66% in 2021). No exacerbations, no steroids or antibiotics in the past year. Albuterol ~2x/wk. Climbs 2 flights with a pause, no chest pain. >4 METs.
Smoking ~1 ppd, ~33 pack-years. Says she'll stop the week before like last time.
No bleeding disorder history, no anticoagulants.
Meds: tiotropium 18 mcg daily, albuterol prn, amlodipine 5. NKDA.

Exam: BP at goal, vitals per flowsheet. Airway unchanged. Heart regular. Lungs with prolonged expiration, no wheeze. No edema.
ECG: NSR, normal, unchanged.
CBC/BMP today.

Impression: acceptable risk for planned low-risk procedure. Same recommendations as 2023: take tiotropium and amlodipine morning of surgery, bring albuterol, early ambulation. Note sent to gyn onc.

documents.title: Operative Report - Gynecologic Oncology
documents.author: gynecologic oncology
documents.body:
OPERATIVE REPORT
Date of surgery: 06/23/2026
Preoperative diagnosis: Squamous cell carcinoma of the posterior vaginal wall, clinical stage I.
Postoperative diagnosis: Same.
Procedure: Wide local excision of posterior vaginal wall lesion (partial vaginectomy).
Anesthesia: General.
Findings: Exam under anesthesia confirmed a 2 cm ulcerated lesion of the posterior vaginal wall, mobile, without paravaginal or rectovaginal septum involvement. Cervix and vulva without lesion.
Description: The lesion was outlined with a 1 cm margin, and the vaginal wall was excised full thickness, preserving the underlying rectovaginal fascia. Specimen oriented and sent. Rectal exam at the end confirmed intact rectal mucosa. The defect was closed primarily. EBL 75 mL. No complications.
Disposition: Discharged home the same day after voiding. Ibuprofen 600 mg q6h prn with food for up to 7 days. Continue home inhalers and amlodipine. Pelvic rest until cleared. Follow-up in 4 weeks.
Allergies: NKDA.

Gynecologic Oncology

documents.title: Post-op Call
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Post-op check-in call, POD 2. Sore but okay; ibuprofen helping, taking it with food. Light pink discharge only, no heavy bleeding, no fever, voiding fine, bowels moving. Breathing at baseline. Not smoking since last Tuesday. Has gyn onc's after-hours number. Post-op visit 7/21.

reports.text:
SPECIMEN: Vagina, posterior wall lesion, wide local excision (oriented).
DIAGNOSIS: Invasive squamous cell carcinoma, p16 block-positive.
   Tumor size: 2.0 cm.
   Depth of invasion: 3 mm.
   Lymphovascular invasion: not identified.
   Margins: all margins negative for carcinoma; closest margin 5 mm.
SYNOPTIC: pT1. FIGO stage I.
reports.conclusion: Posterior vaginal wall invasive squamous cell carcinoma, p16-positive, 2.0 cm, 3 mm depth of invasion, margins negative. FIGO stage I.

documents.body: Thank you. Healing ok, sore when I sit too long. Relieved.

documents.title: Gynecologic Oncology Post-op Visit
documents.author: gynecologic oncology
documents.body:
GYNECOLOGIC ONCOLOGY - POST-OP 07/21/2026
Four weeks after wide local excision of a posterior vaginal wall SCC. Recovering well; off ibuprofen for two weeks. Spotting stopped after the first week. No pain with bowel movements, no fever.

Exam: Vaginal incision healed, no granulation or separation. No groin adenopathy. Vulva unchanged with healed right scar.

Pathology reviewed: invasive SCC, p16-positive, 2.0 cm, DOI 3 mm, no LVSI, margins negative (closest 5 mm). FIGO stage I.

Plan: No adjuvant therapy. Surveillance every 3 months with history and exam, alternating with her gynecologist as before, given two HPV-associated lower genital tract cancers. Next visit here in October. Pelvic rest lifted. Asked again to stop smoking; she says she is trying.

Gynecologic Oncology
